name: BuildingModelPlaceholder
intent: A dependency-free CSS-3D building placeholder (one extruded box per floor, drag-to-orbit, click-to-select) that stands in for a real BIM / 3D model when one isn't available yet.
when: A building's floors need a 3D-ish preview but no BIM model exists
Selecting a floor from a lightweight 3D stand-in

chooseOver.because: BuildingModelPlaceholder is a zero-dependency stand-in used only until a real model is wired up

notes: authored during the develop merge reconciliation

props.name: floors
props.description: Floors ordered top → bottom (roof first). One extruded box is stacked per floor.

props.name: ...props
props.description: All standard HTML attributes are supported.

usage: Use BuildingModelPlaceholder to enhance your user interface. This component provides a consistent, accessible, and well-designed solution for this use case.
BuildingModelPlaceholder integrates seamlessly with other components in the design system. Follow the established patterns and guidelines to ensure consistency across your application.

anatomy.description: BuildingModelPlaceholder is composed of the following parts:

bestPractices.title: Use semantic props
bestPractices.description: Use the component's built-in props rather than className overrides.

bestPractices.title: Don't override core styles
bestPractices.description: Avoid using className to override the component's fundamental styling.

bestPractices.title: Provide accessible labels
bestPractices.description: Include proper ARIA labels for screen reader users.

bestPractices.title: Don't skip accessibility
bestPractices.description: Never omit accessibility attributes for interactive components.

bestPractices.title: Handle all states
bestPractices.description: Account for loading, error, empty, and success states.

bestPractices.title: Don't ignore edge cases
bestPractices.description: Avoid showing broken UI when data is missing or loading.
